subject: Charge modeling & price-sensitivity snapshot for Nimbus - post-demo recap
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Rogers <liam.rogers@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Charge modeling & price-sensitivity snapshot for Nimbus - post-demo recap

Hi Liam — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so everything's in one place.

Key takeaways from the demo:
- Nimbus expects a bursty product mix (search & summarization) with a heavy tail of high-completion tokens per request.
- Compliance: data residency in us-west for PII-containing logs.
- Integration: will start with API + streaming; possible Dedicated pool if latency/throughput targets tighten.

Cost/qualification items we need from you to model a pricing proposal:
1) Monthly token volumes (separate prompt vs completion if possible) — rough ranges ok (e.g., 50–200M /mo).
2) Committed vs burst behavior: committed baseline and expected peak multiplier (e.g., 3x).
3) Target unit economics: what are you thinking for $/1M tokens baseline and aspirational ceiling?
4) Preferred model families (OpenAI-like, Anthropic, or open model variants) — this impacts host parity and quantization paths.
5) Procurement timeline & PO contact (we'll include a reserved capacity option with term pricing).

Preliminary benchmark context (for orientation only):
- OpenAI: baseline host parity for gpt-like LLMs we commonly see pricing in the $200–350 / 1M token range for higher capability endpoints (public list rates vary).
- Anthropic: comparable band for chat-style workloads, slightly higher for some Claude variants on equivalent capability.
- Open-model hosts (HF/Replicate/Lambda): wide range. For quantized, batched inference you can see unit costs that approach $100–180 / 1M but tradeoffs on latency and feature parity (tool-calling, streaming).

What Redwood can model for you in the proposal:
- Per-1M token scenarios across three model families (high-accuracy, balanced, low-cost quantized)
- Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted-on-demand math (showing effective $/1M at different commitment tiers)
- Sensitivity sweep: how $/1M changes with prefix caching, batching, and KV cache reuse assumptions.

Attached: "nimbus_multiproduct_volume_table.xlsx" — template if you want to drop in expected volumes, and a quick Redwood benchmarking PDF "redwood_1M_unit_comps.pdf" with our visible host comps (anonymized).

Next steps / asks:
- Can you reply with the volume ranges and a target $/1M (even a single reference number helps) by Tue 10/6?
- If procurement wants a sample SOW / reserved-capacity Term sheet, loop them in and Ben will prepare a draft.

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the sensitivity matrix live.

Thanks —
Hannah

From: Liam Rogers <liam.rogers@nimbus.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.k@nimbus.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Charge modeling & price-sensitivity snapshot for Nimbus - post-demo recap

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear template. Answers below (inline to your asks).

> 1) Monthly token volumes (separate prompt vs completion if possible)
We expect month 1 of production to be ~1.0B tokens (aggregate). Long-term steady-state estimate is ~3.5B tokens / month across products. Rough split: prompts ~150M, completions ~850M in month 1; steady-state prompts ~500M / completions ~3.0B.

> 2) Committed vs burst behavior
We can commit to a 750M tokens / month baseline for an initial 12-month term, with ability to burst up to 4x for 48-hour peaks. Bursts are primarily during feature rollouts.

> 3) Target unit economics: what are you thinking for $/1M tokens baseline and aspirational ceiling?
Internal target is $150 / 1M tokens as our preferred benchmark. We can stretch to $220/1M if that unlocks lower latency SLA or feature parity (e.g., streaming + tool-calls). If you can show a path to ~120–140/1M with committed reserved capacity + quantized open-model mix, that would be interesting.

> 4) Preferred model families
We want a hybrid approach: majority on a balanced open-model variant (cost-sensitivity) with fallback to higher-capability hosted models for certain flows (safety-critical summarization).

> 5) Procurement timeline & PO contact
Procurement contact: procurement@nimbus.ai (cc'd). We are aiming to finalize terms by 10/20.

I've attached our internal volume forecast spreadsheet ("nimbus_monthly_forecast_q4_q1.xlsx"). We'll need a proposal that shows: 1) on-demand hosted pricing, 2) 12-mo reserved capacity schedule with tiered $/1M at 750M / 1.5B / 3.5B commitments, and 3) a pilot scope for 30 days at 0 cost to validate latency.

Liam
Liam Rogers
Head of Product, Nimbus.ai
liam.rogers@nimbus.ai
(415) 555-0339

Liam — great, thanks for the detail and the internal spreadsheet (we have it). Short summary and proposed next steps: 

Quick synthesis of your targets vs our benchmark thinking:
- Nimbus steady-state ~3.5B /mo: means material scale where reserved pricing yields the largest delta.
- Your preferred $150 / 1M sits between typical hosted list rates and optimized quantized open-hosts; feasible with a mixed routing strategy and 12-mo commit.
- Stretch target (~120–140 / 1M) aligns with aggressive quantized open-model routing + caching and a dedicated pool for peak-sensitive flows. Tradeoffs: higher tail latency and some feature gaps (e.g., function-calling parity).

What we'll deliver by Tue 10/6:
1) A pricing sensitivity matrix PDF that shows effective $/1M at the commitment tiers you asked for (750M / 1.5B / 3.5B) across three model-mix scenarios. (attachment: redwood_1M_unit_comps.pdf)
2) A draft Term Sheet for a 12-mo reserved capacity option (Ben will author the commercial table and term discounts).
3) Pilot plan: 30-day pilot scope, KPIs for latency, token instrumentation, and an initial SLO for failure/fallback behavior.

If Procurement would like a single consolidated spreadsheet we can populate your "nimbus_monthly_forecast_q4_q1.xlsx" with modeled rows (I can drop a completed version into the HubSpot record). Ben — can you prepare the Term Sheet draft and the per-tier math?

Procurement — we'll follow up via the DocuSign link in the HubSpot opportunity once the commercial table is ready. Proposed time to review the sensitivity matrix together: Wed 10/7 10:00 PT (30 min). Does that work?

Thanks — talk soon.
Hannah
